t: #3895 Count Digit Appearances — String Count vs Arithmetic Extraction
o: Count occurrences of a given digit across the decimal representations of all array elements. Trivially done by converting to strings, or by repeatedly dividing by ten. Example: [12,54,32,22] with digit 2 gives 1 + 0 + 1 + 2 = 4.
k: String conversion plus substring counting is the shortest path.
Arithmetic digit extraction (mod/divide by 10) avoids string allocation.
Since nums[i] >= 1, leading zeros never occur, so digit 0 can only appear internally.

a.i: Convert each number to its decimal string and count occurrences of the target digit character.
s: Map the digit to its character.
For each number, count matches in its string form.
a.t: O(total number of digits) — linear in input size.
a.sp: O(digits of one number) for the temporary string.

a.i: Strip digits from the low end with % 10 and / 10, comparing each to the target — no string allocations.
s: For each number, loop while it is positive.
Compare num % 10 to digit and count matches.

w: Both approaches are fine at these constraints; prefer arithmetic extraction in performance-sensitive settings. Edge case: digit 0 never matches the leading digit since inputs are >= 1. Follow-up: count digit occurrences across the entire range [1, n] — that requires the classical digit-DP / positional counting formula.
